locations.name: 2 Copper Reads
locations.summary: 2 Copper Reads is a shop that, as its name suggests, sells books for only two copper pieces. The stories they sell are compilations from various books that their owner, Horace Drimvon, has assembled page by page, and sometimes political or religious content appears from the diverse works he combines into a single new w...

locations.name: A Magical Touch
locations.summary: A Magical Touch is a shop selling magical items of dubious nature, located in the back alleys of the Grand Bazaar. Its owner, Erandi, stocks a variety of glitches, such as bags with extradimensional space that are as large as a normal bag, or wands that stop casting magic after a single use.

locations.name: Absalom Academy of Law
locations.summary: The Absalom Academy of Law is one of its most influential educational institutions outside the nation, attracting students from as far away as Tian Xia who travel there to learn the city's laws and how to manage a bureaucratic body as large as Absalom's.

locations.name: Absalom Chirurgeon Dispatch
locations.summary: The Absalom Chirurgeon Dispatch is where the doctors, physicians, and healers of the Westgate district meet. It operates similarly to the practices of smaller towns where there is no hospital, and the doctor travels to the patient's home when called.

locations.name: Absalom Harbor
locations.summary: Absalom Harbor refers to the water bounded by Absalom city to the north and Pilot Island and the Flotsam Graveyard to the south at its mouth. The harbour is overlooked by the Starwatch Keep to the east and Fort Tempest to the west.

locations.name: Absalom Lighthouse
locations.summary: Absalom Lighthouse is located on Pilot Island at the center of Absalom's Flotsam Graveyard. It is a famed piece of architecture built under the command of the god Aroden.

locations.name: Absalom Menagerie
locations.summary: The Absalom Menagerie is a park where a wide variety of animals live in climate-controlled enclosures behind magical walls designed to reduce the danger to visitors.

locations.name: Absalom Mint
locations.summary: The Absalom Mint, located near Azlanti Keep in Absalom's Wise Quarter that produces much of the city's coinage—a function that, due to the City at the Center of the World's outsized influence on trade and commerce, literally and figuratively shapes money across the Inner Sea region and beyond.

locations.name: Ahnkamen Estate
locations.summary: The Ahnkamen Estate is a beautiful Osirian-style manor with magnificent gardens that are frequently visited for the parties held every two weeks. These are the most fun in town, and no one realizes that beneath them lie cellars with temples to Yog-Sothoth and other Outer Gods, the extensive residence of Mother Jackal,...

locations.name: Al'Hakam Estate
locations.summary: The Al'Hakam Estate is an impressive manor house on the edge of The Coins, near the Ascendant Court. Its grandeur is understandable, as it is not only the home of the influential merchant Aaqir al'Hakam but also of Emir Thalzar Gaatan, ambassador of Qadira.

locations.name: Alyssia's
locations.summary: Alyssia's is a very expensive but extremely beautiful teahouse in the Ivy District that caters to elven tastes and is run by Lady Alyssia. The hallways are curved, giving the impression of an aiudara, and although most of the staff are elves, any customer is welcome as long as they have the money and the decorum to beh...

locations.name: Anandari Block
locations.summary: The Anandari Block is a Westgate neighborhood populated mostly by people of vudrani descent, and the architecture and food offered in the area reflect this style.

locations.name: Antler Lodge
locations.summary: Antler Lodge is the temple of Erastil, located in the urban city of Absalom, offering respite in its gardens to those who long for a rustic life. In the Eastgate district, a modest two-story structure can be seen with aesthetically pleasing wooden atlers at the entrance.

locations.name: Arbor Ward
locations.summary: The Arbor Ward is a neighborhood in the Ivy District that boasts some of the city's finest restaurants, whose culinary recipes are tasted by travelers who will take them back to their nations across the Inner Sea, expanding their influence.

locations.name: Arboretum Arcanis
locations.summary: The Arboretum Arcanis once contained a wonderland of exotic fruit and blossoms from beyond Golarion. It was housed in a magical crystal dome in the Precipice Quarter in Absalom.

locations.name: Arcanamirium
locations.summary: The Arcanamirium is not only the largest and oldest school in Absalom, but quite possibly the most prestigious arcane magic academy in the entire Inner Sea region of Golarion.

locations.name: Arcane Antiquary
locations.summary: Arcane Antiquary is a stall that sells ancient magical relics at high prices. These relics can be found cheaper elsewhere, but their age lends them added historical value, attracting collectors.

locations.name: Archerus Manor
locations.summary: Archerus Manor is the residence of one of the Inner Sea's most famous artists, the painter Endrik Archerus, who lives in a massive stone tower visible throughout the district.

locations.name: Asad's Keep
locations.summary: Asad's Keep is one of the many crumbling siege castles in the Cairnlands outside of Absalom. It was a Qadiran fortress built centuries ago by the ambitious Taliq Asad, who tried to take the city of Absalom. The sturdy keep sank into the earth around the time Asad's efforts failed.

locations.name: Avatectura Museum
locations.summary: The Avatectura Museum in the Wise Quarter offers city archives dating from all eras, although its popular style is due to its curator, Dhauken Tor, who manages it.

locations.name: Avenue of the Hopeful
locations.summary: The Avenue of the Hopeful is a winding street in Absalom's Ascendant Court and a busy market catering to those fascinated by the Test of the Starstone: hopefuls, followers, worshippers, and the merchants, pickpockets, and charlatans who hope to make money from them.

locations.name: Aysepir's Astounded Abyss
locations.summary: Aysepir's Astounded Abyss is a carnival show of unusual, and often disturbing, beings in the Puddles district of Absalom. Despite having the trappings of fiction and making extraordinary claims, its employees are exactly what they are presented to be—beings of sometimes immense power afflicted by curses or misfortune,...

locations.name: Azari Palace
locations.summary: The Azari Palace is an ossified remnant of the period when worship of Aroden was a prominent feature of life in Absalom, before his death and the dawn of the Age of Lost Omens.

locations.name: Azlanti Keep
locations.summary: Azlanti Keep is a stone fortress in the city of Absalom that is so massive, it is considered by some to be its own city district, although it is not one officially and does not formally belong to any other city district.

locations.name: Bail House
locations.summary: The Bail House is the headquarters of the Token Guard, the district watch of the Coins district of Absalom. It gets its name from the guards' habit of jailing everyone present at a disturbance and holding them until they can post bail, which is usually 1 copper piece per arrest.

locations.name: Band of the Palm Headquarters
locations.summary: The Band of the Palm Headquarters is where the Bloody Barbers criminal gang gathers for their operations throughout the city. Under the guise of the Band of the Palm, a union of chimney sweeps, garbage collectors, and cleaners operate out of this series of buildings that include offices, sleeping quarters, bankrupt bus...

locations.name: Bank of Absalom
locations.summary: The Bank of Absalom has a far-reaching power, influencing trade and finance beyond the City at the Centre of the World across the Inner Sea region. From the Bank of Absalom, its bankers can influence the flow of trade and commerce by adjusting interest rates, approving (or not) massive loans, and issuing debt collectio...

locations.name: Barghest's Bin
locations.summary: The Barghest's Bin is a shop in the Grand Bazaar that proudly invites treasure hunters to venture into dangerous dungeons and bring back treasures to sell. The owner, Omira Descinaria, points out potential loot-filled dungeons to adventurers, and if they don't return, her conscience is clear, for there's always someone...

locations.name: Barque Bazaar
locations.summary: The Barque Bazaar is a floating business where several barges have joined together, and merchants sell their foreign goods to customers all along the Absalom coast.

locations.name: Barterfall
locations.summary: Barterfall is a neighborhood in the Precipice Quarter, named for its economy and precarious living conditions. It's one of the least dangerous parts of the district, though that's not saying much.

locations.name: Bartie's Barges
locations.summary: Bartie's Barges is a shipyard in The Docks run by halflings affiliated with Darabelle Fairwind's Pilot's Union. They typically build small, flat-bottomed boats.

locations.name: Bedelsby's Bid-A-Lot
locations.summary: Bedelsby's Bid-A-Lot is an auction house where works of art and restored objects are put up for auction by the halfling Alexius Bedelsby. Most of the proceeds go to help the less fortunate in Absalom, which gives the establishment the respect of the community.

locations.name: Beldrin's Tower
locations.summary: Beldrin's Tower, sometimes known as the Tower of the Broken Shield, is the most famous monument in the Precipice Quarter of Absalom. Originally part of a three-spire magic academy established by the wizard Beldrin, it suffered considerable damage after the earthquake of 4698 AR.

locations.name: Bellwether Lodge
locations.summary: The Bellwether Lodge is a shop with wooden walls and a red roof where you can not only buy hunting weapons but also have a yard where customers can try out the bows they purchase.

locations.name: Beneath the Docks
locations.summary: Beneath the Docks is a neighborhood beneath the wooden planks of the district, inhabited by the area's poorest residents, those with criminal connections, or those who prefer to live as close to the water as possible.

locations.name: Beragel's Fur and Feathers
locations.summary: Beragel's Fur and Feathers is a pet shop run by Beragel Tindertales, offering animals from all over Golarion, as well as food and specialized enclosures to keep them happy.

locations.name: Besmara's Boardwalk
locations.summary: Besmara's Boardwalk is located in the eastern part of The Docks, where visitors can participate in carnival games, purchase souvenirs of their visit to the city, or enjoy street food from the various food stalls.

locations.name: Black Mask
locations.summary: The Black Mask is a high-end costume shop in Absalom's Ascendant Court, carrying masks, cloaks, and everything from common disguise kits to costumes used by parade or theater performers.

locations.name: Black Whale
locations.summary: Established in 4693 AR, the Black Whale is a prison on the western part of the Flotsam Graveyard intended for the most notorious or politically sensitive prisoners too dangerous to be kept in the Brine in Puddles. The prison consists of six beached ships, bolted to it with long chains and each lashed together.

locations.name: Blackblade's
locations.summary: Blackblade's is a successful fighting academy where former pathfinder and mercenary Benkhal Blackblade instructs his students in combat for five pieces of silver twice a week.

locations.name: Blackfingers Temple
locations.summary: Blackfingers Temple is the primary place of worship to Norgorber in the city of Absalom and is the only known place of worship that exclusively reveres Norgorber's Blackfingers aspect.

locations.name: Blackhill's
locations.summary: Blackhill's is a tavern in Eastgate that at first glance looks like a thatched roof a foot off the ground, leading to a constantly ventilated cellar where Dege Blackhill creates his famous spicy drinks, popular with those from Numeria.

locations.name: Blakros Museum
locations.summary: The Blakros Museum was the former stronghold of a mad astrologer and wizard named Ralzeros the Overwatched in the early history of Absalom. The mage constructed the building from a solid block of volcanic stone with the aid of dark, alien powers.

locations.name: Bloom Cabaret
locations.summary: The Bloom Cabaret is a cafe on one of the busiest streets of the district, and behind one of its private rooms lies the entrance to archives used by the Ordaire of Goode Standing, composed of wealthy socialites with a hunger for occult and esoteric knowledge.

locations.name: Blue Tower
locations.summary: The Blue Tower is the tallest building within the city walls of Absalom, and the third-tallest building in the whole city. Residents across the city use both the Blue Tower, the northwestern Spire of Nex, and the peaks of the Kortos Mounts as navigational landmarks.

locations.name: Boneglutton Pit
locations.summary: The Boneglutton Pit is a hole where the guards of Beldrin's Bluff dumped corpses and rubble while attempting to reclaim the district after the earthquake, but the stench and swarms of flies became unbearable.

locations.name: Bonekeep
locations.summary: Created over 200 years ago by the necromancer Volzaras, an exile from Geb, Bonekeep refers more specifically to the heavily warded dungeon beneath the ruined siege castle.

locations.name: Brazen Arch
locations.summary: See also: First Siege of Absalom The Brazen Arch (also known as the Brazen Gate) was a massive teleportation portal built on the orders of the minotaur warlord Voradni Voon for his invasion of Absalom in 23 AR.

locations.name: Brine
locations.summary: For other meanings of "Brine", please see Brine (disambiguation). The Brine is an imposing stone prison house located in the Puddles district in Absalom. Lady Seichya of House Tevineg serves as the prison's head warden.

locations.name: Broadfoot Marshals Station House
locations.summary: Broadfoot Marshals Station House is a base for a private firefighting brigade in The Docks district of Absalom. Under the instruction of the dwarven engineer Bagara Broadfoot, they use water carts that, through pedals, can create pressure to expel water and extinguish fires, which are quite dangerous in a district made...

locations.name: Broken Bastion
locations.summary: The Broken Bastion was a clock tower maintained by a mystical sect obsessed with time, but three centuries ago the structure and the temporal artifact it protected were destroyed by the dragon Maejeryx Steeleye.

locations.name: Bunk Fields
locations.summary: The Bunk Fields is an area in Azlanti Keep in Absalom of row after row of simple bunks that is mostly abandoned unless the city is under siege, occasionally used for illicit gambling, recreation, or other activities.

locations.name: Cacaspal's
locations.summary: Cacaspal's is a cart that stops in one of the alleys of the Grand Bazaar every week to sell garden fertilizers, although its creator, Rudrich Caspal, secretly sells poisons after learning a bit of alchemy from a follower of Norgorber.

locations.name: Cairnlands
locations.summary: See also: History of Absalom The inevitable result of over four millennia of warfare and countless unsuccessful sieges on the walls of Absalom, the region around the city is known as the Cairnlands and is filled with ruined siege engines and battlements.

locations.name: Castle Blakros
locations.summary: Castle Blakros is an imposing black stone structure in the Petal District. The Blakros family lives surrounded by 20-foot-high walls and beautiful gardens near a natural lake.

locations.name: Catacombs (Absalom)
locations.summary: The Catacombs of Absalom are a labyrinthine network of passageways near the Starstone Cathedral where early followers of Aroden are buried. Pilgrims can pass through one of these passages carrying a candle and receiving a coin bearing the image of one of those buried there.

locations.name: Catfish Salvage Solutions
locations.summary: Catfish Salvage Solutions is a hard-to-find establishment, as this open-air pavilion resembles an art exhibit with towers of gears more than anything else, serving more as a shortcut than a shop.

locations.name: Cats and Caboodle
locations.summary: Cats and Caboodle is a general store which, after its owner Hierisa made a deal with Josie's Kennel, has a back room decorated for cats to play with customers. Since opening this section, business has been booming, and she directs customers to Josie's if they want to adopt one of the cats.

locations.name: Catwalk Corridors
locations.summary: The Catwalk Corridors is a neighborhood on the roofs of The Puddles made up of wooden bridges connecting the houses, used by the more agile residents and goblins who race each other, laughing at those who have to walk through the streets below, getting wet.The most skilled runners are hired by different factions fighti...

locations.name: Cayden's Hall
locations.summary: Cayden's Hall in the Ascendant Court district of Absalom is a large, boisterous meadhall and temple of Cayden Cailean, built of wood as was the original meadhall from which Cayden set out to take the Test of the Starstone.

locations.name: Chamber Grove
locations.summary: The Chamber Grove is where the Ivy District Council meets to discuss matters concerning, above all, the district's theater scene, as this is of paramount importance to the district.

locations.name: Chapel of Shadow
locations.summary: The Chapel of Shadow is an abandoned temple of Nethys which the residents of The Puddles believe to be haunted, as they see figures moving in the darkness at night. The Onyx Alliance uses the location to reliably transition from Shadow Absalom to the Universe.

locations.name: Chelaxian embassy
locations.summary: This article refers to the Chelaxian embassy in Absalom. For the embassy in Bloodcove, see Chelaxian Embassy (Bloodcove). The Chelaxian embassy in Absalom is housed in the former temple of Aroden, which was leased by the Grand Council after the god's death.

locations.name: Church of Asmodeus (Absalom)
locations.summary: The Church of Asmodeus is one of the youngest building of the Ascendant Court, the religious heart of Absalom, with the previous high temple to Asmodeus having been burned to the ground during the so-called "Devil's Night Uprising" in 4698 AR.

locations.name: Church of the Muted God
locations.summary: The Church of the Muted God is dedicated to this would-be god of the Failed, who perished during the Test of the Starstone but still has followers. The Muted God provides no divine power or guidance, and the members of this benevolent organization are becoming more of a criminal group than a religious congregation.

locations.name: Clockwork Cathedral
locations.summary: The Clockwork Cathedral, the youngest of Absalom's Great Schools, specializes in the studies of mechanical engineering and constructs. The Cathedral is located in the Merchants' Quarter, within The Coins district of Absalom.

locations.name: College of Mysteries
locations.summary: The College of Mysteries (formerly known as the House of Secrets) is the oldest school of magic in Absalom and is located in the Petal District. The college has a superb reputation in the city and is favored by a number of organisations, such the Javelin Gallery, whom they aid by enchanting weapons.

locations.name: Concerned Residents' Union
locations.summary: The Concerned Residents' Union is Eastgate's second council, unrecognized as official. However, because the district is such a close-knit community, decisions made by the residents are often final, while official recognition is merely a formality.

locations.name: Concurrent Currency
locations.summary: Concurrent Currency is a currency exchange business run by the charismatic Darelli Gammathumalshire and the affable Bagwell Thomkin in The Docks district. The shop has been operating for over 20 years and has acquired not only current coins but also antique ones of great interest to collectors.

locations.name: Consortium Citadel
locations.summary: The Consortium Citadel is located in south-central Diobel. This dockside building housing the Kortos Consortium was the tallest building in Diobel until the Hall of the Teriarch was created.

locations.name: Consulate of the Platinum Band
locations.summary: The Consulate of the Platinum Band is a temple dedicated to Apsu where his non-draconic followers gather and help others. Although the faith isn't widely understood by the residents of The Puddles, they won't refuse the magical assistance offered. The building also houses archives on the region's dragon lore.

locations.name: Counterfeit Peak
locations.summary: Counterfeit Peak is one of the siege castles that attacked Absalom, created during the Siege of Krakens and Kings. This siege was an internal battle between the Cult of the Hawk and the Blue Lords.

locations.name: Court of Black Paper
locations.summary: The Court of Black Paper in Absalom is, in nearly equal parts, a powerful cartel-like law firm, a cutthroat school of legal studies, and a cult of Norgorber. Its ranking members are known as priest-advocates and are led by Senior Priest-Advocate Samel Maleagant, who has a reputation as the city's most prominent lawyer.

locations.name: Craft Vaults
locations.summary: The Craft Vaults are a series of workshops, stables, and armories in Azlanti Keep in Absalom that provides weapons and supplies for the First Guard. Nominally governed by Quartermaster Lord Yuvin Vatir of House Damaq, in practice, the sector was overseen by master craftswoman Chun Hye-Seung before her promotion, while...

locations.name: Crescent Manor
locations.summary: The Crescent Manor was the residence of the information broker Grandmaster Torch, who left the city and vanished into the shadows to some unknown location. Sometimes the lights are seen on upstairs, fueling rumors of his imminent return.

locations.name: Crestwatch
locations.summary: Crestwatch is a structure with a 100-foot minaret in the middle of The Docks that serves as the administrative center of the district. The east wing is used by the Harbor Guard, which patrols and fights crime, and the west wing is used by the Docks Council, which creates the laws and taxes that apply to ships docking i...

locations.name: Crimson Coin
locations.summary: Crimson Coin is a bustling two-story tavern and gambling house located in the Foreign Quarter in the city of Absalom. It was one of the bars at which the Pathfinder Society was founded on 23 Desnus, 4307 AR.

locations.name: Critters Galore
locations.summary: Critters Galore is the third pet shop Rizeka has run; the first two were shut down by the authorities after an incident in which a salamander set fire to a customer's house. Cages and jars fill the shelves, containing oozes, spiders, and even small elementals, all for sale under dubious legality.

locations.name: Crystal Creations
locations.summary: Crystal Creations is a glassblowing shop that sees a lot of customers but little business, as it's the Crowsworn gang's base of operations beneath it. The Crowsworn move through tunnels built by the dwarves of Westerhold millennia ago.

locations.name: Crystal Palace (Mudhaven)
locations.summary: The Crystal Palace is a structure in Mudhaven where the Dod's Filchers operate. Its founder was the aiuvarin Malina Dod, who led the group, but after her mysterious disappearance, a pair of halfling twins took control.

locations.name: Dacilane Academy
locations.summary: Dacilane Academy, formerly known as the Urbane District Academy, is a school for children of Pathfinders stationed in the Grand Lodge of Absalom's Foreign Quarter and is located a few blocks from the Pathfinder Society's headquarters.

locations.name: Dacilane Manor
locations.summary: The Dacilane Manor is an impressive four-story structure in the Ivy District surrounded by magnificent gardens, where Lady Miranda Dacilane resides. The house is decorated with chelaxian and asmodean ornamentation.

locations.name: Daltus Academy
locations.summary: The Daltus Academy is a boarding school that occupies an entire block of the district where its campus, dormitories, and classrooms are located. Students at this academy are often involved in fights and are viewed unfavorably by the other residents of the district who tend to avoid them.

locations.name: Damaq Palace
locations.summary: The Damaq Palace lives up to its name, for this ostentatious structure rivals many palaces of Inner Sea kings, its facade frequently redecorated simply because House Damaq tires of seeing the same thing everyday.

locations.name: Dark Archive
locations.summary: This article describes the Pathfinder Society vault. For the faction, see Dark Archive (faction). For the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game sourcebook, see Dark Archive (sourcebook). The Dark Archive is a location in the deepest vaults of the Pathfinder Society headquarters in Absalom.

locations.name: Darkgate
locations.summary: The Darkgate is a fissure in the Precipice Quarter, created during the earthquake that devastated much of the district. Months after it opened, undead and monsters emerged from the fissure and still roam the city streets.

locations.name: Dawnflower Library
locations.summary: The Dawnflower Library is a temple of Sarenrae and library located on 10 Dawnflower Street in the town of Otari, on the southern coast of the Isle of Kortos. Its high priestess is Vandy Banderdash, a talkative halfling woman.

locations.name: Deckland Vaults
locations.summary: The Deckland Vaults are an underground complex beneath the House Deckland estate in Eastgate, which contained compromising notes about Absalom's defenses and weaknesses. These notes led to the family's exile from the city, though some remained until they were recovered by the Pathfinder Society in 4710 AR.

locations.name: Delirium's Tangle
locations.summary: The Delirium's Tangle lies deep within the Ivy District, a constantly shifting labyrinth constructed by an elf obsessed with immortality after witnessing his human family die repeatedly. The labyrinth defies the laws of physics, and getting lost within it is incredibly easy.

locations.name: Devil's Advocates
locations.summary: The Devil's Advocates was as of 4708 AR a small Chelaxian slave brokerage in the Coins district of Absalom. It specialized in well-trained, skilled, and obedient slaves from Cheliax. Most had accepted slavery as a punishment for some crime, knowing that their families will suffer for their rebellion.

locations.name: Devil's Own
locations.summary: The Devil's Own is a shipyard in the Docks district of the city of Absalom. The shipyard specializes in war galleys used by Absalom's navy and sold to the markets throughout the Inner Sea. Its owner, Lord Archych of House Dureanz is a loyal Chelaxian.

locations.name: Devil's Pier
locations.summary: Devil's Pier is at the extreme southern end of Diobel's harbour, and gets its name from the habit of Chelaxian ships to dock at Diobel to avoid the delays imposed on them in Absalom. These traders first make a large bribe to Lord Avid of House Arnsen , and he permitted them to construct the pier solely for their use.

locations.name: Devils' Garden
locations.summary: Devil's Garden, also known as Cheliax's Garden, is a neighborhood in the Foreign Quarter where both exiles from the nation and agents of House Thrune live together, enjoying wine, opera, and the company of each other most of which cannot return to their homeland.

locations.name: District Courthouse (Ascendant Court)
locations.summary: The District Courthouse of the Ascendant Court is where the district's less serious criminal trials are held, overseen by a trio of elderly judges of Abadar. Their judgments are fair, but the work here is usually quite slow, with a waiting list for filing a complaint or processing a grievance.

locations.name: District Courthouse (Eastgate)
locations.summary: The District Courthouse in Eastgate has a reputation for the compassion shown by its judges and prosecutors, which makes sense given the close-knit nature of the district, but some of its sentences border on negligence.

locations.name: District Courthouse (Foreign Quarter)
locations.summary: The District Courthouse for the Foreign Quarter is a stone building where its judges are renowned for their knowledge of foreign law, and most crimes are tried in its jurisdiction because they are committed by foreigners. The Sleepless Suns maintain a presence in the building, assisting as bailiffs when needed.

locations.name: District Courthouse (Ivy District)
locations.summary: The District Courthouse in the Ivy District is one of the smallest in all of Absalom, having not been expanded for years. Because of this, huge crowds gather outside to watch the trials and performers, of course, take advantage of this opportunity to put on shows that even distract the judges from reaching their verdic...

locations.name: District Courthouse (Precipice Quarter)
locations.summary: The District Courthouse in the Precipice Quarter, like many parts of the district, was abandoned following the earthquake that shook the city. The judges sealed the building with barricades after wrongfully executing Jarbin Mord, and his spirit is said to haunt the white marble halls of this crumbling four-story buildi...

locations.name: District Courthouse (The Coins)
locations.summary: The District Courthouse in The Coins is located in the western part of the district, just outside the Grand Bazaar. It is in this building that district justice should be administered, but although several corrupt judges have been removed in recent years, there are always people willing to reduce sentences or declare i...

locations.name: District Courthouse (The Docks)
locations.summary: The District Courthouse in The Docks handles cases brought by both the energetic and rough dockworkers and the reckless and unwary foreigners who don't even know the city's laws. The court system has a reputation for being quite chaotic and unpredictable.

locations.name: District Courthouse (Westgate)
locations.summary: The Westgate District Courthouse is a large, four-winged building where trials for the district are held and the prosecutor's offices are located. In the middle of the wings is a huge pool where, by tradition, suspects are brought to the edge to see their reflection in this natural mirror and clear their thoughts befor...

locations.name: Doctor Mirchan's Haven for Better Being
locations.summary: Doctor Mirchan's Haven for Better Being is a store that sells health tips from Geridem Luvlassian, along with every herbal pillow, sunscreen, and sleep-inducing recipe imaginable.

locations.name: Dracori's Sensory Wares
locations.summary: Dracori's Sensory Wares, or Emporium, is a stall serving the strangest yet most enticing street foods in the Grand Bazaar. The aromas of spices and dishes from around the world fill the shop, and although Fribinella Dracori initially targeted a gnome clientele seeking novel experiences to help them avoid Bleaching, the...

locations.name: Drownyard
locations.summary: The Drownyard is a location in the city of Absalom, in the (now mostly destroyed) Precipice Quarter. Before the terrible earthquake of 4698 AR, the Precipice Quarter (formerly known as Beldrin's Bluff) was known as the Tri-Towers Yard, the premier finishing school for children of the rich and powerful.

locations.name: Eagle Garrison Fort
locations.summary: The Eagle Garrison Fort is a fortress of the Eagle Garrison located in the northern Kortos Mounts foothills, about 100 miles' travel from Diobel on land by way of Meravon.

locations.name: Eastgate Hall
locations.summary: Eastgate Hall is an ornate stone structure that once served a group of adventurers fighting against the corruption spread by Rovagug's followers. Today, it is used by the Eastgate Council, which meets monthly to resolve issues arising in the district.

locations.name: El Raja Key
locations.summary: The El Raja Key is one of the massive abandoned siege castles located in the Cairnlands outside the walls of the city of Absalom. It was first catalogued for the Pathfinder Society in 4323 AR by the legendary Durvin Gest, and explored by Venture-Captain Shevala Iorae, who recorded her findings in Volume 36✝︎ of the Pat...

locations.name: Embassy Building
locations.summary: The Embassy Building in Magnimar is set aside for officially invited ambassadors from other countries. Many nations rejected the offer, but those who accepted exchanged functionaries and also receive lowered tariffs and increased trade.

locations.name: Embassy of New Thassilon
locations.summary: The Embassy of New Thassilon, located in the Foreign Quarter, represents the interests of Eurythnia and Edasseril in Absalom. During its first year of operation, both navion agents cooperated with their stone giant allies to renovate a dilapidated building into a magnificent embassy.

locations.name: Embrey's Armory
locations.summary: Embrey's Armory is no ordinary shop, as here the legendary blacksmith Engleton Embrey forges weapons and armor of such quality that one might have to travel to other planes to find better.

locations.name: Emporium Impossible
locations.summary: The Emporium Impossible is one of Absalom's most curious markets, located within a demiplane constructed by the mysterious Namira. Only those she permits—the city's nobles and wealthy—are allowed entry.

locations.name: Endiron School
locations.summary: The Endiron School in Eastgate is a school founded by a noble family with the aim of using words to resolve conflicts between people. To this end, the institution places great emphasis on languages, and its students must know two non-native languages ​​before graduating.

locations.name: Erastil Club
locations.summary: The Erastil Club is the largest hunting lodge in Absalom, boasting an altar where its select members offer a prayer to the god of the hunt before leaving the city in pursuit of their prey. For a fee, anyone can become a member, but they must prove their hunting skills to advance in the ranks.

locations.name: Erastil's Alehouse
locations.summary: Erastil's Alehouse is a popular establishment run by clergymen of Erastil on the edge of the Avenue of the Hopeful, so there is plenty of traffic to offer courage in the form of beer to those trying to become gods.

locations.name: Erran Tower
locations.summary: The Erran Tower is one of the aeon towers that Aroden placed around the Isle of Kortos. The tower is a 300-foot-tall mudbrick step pyramid with a flat top. The tower is located on the east side of the Isle of Erran, and is responsible for magically giving life to the area.

locations.name: Estate of Yargos Gill
locations.summary: The Estate of Yargos Gill is the beautiful residence of one of Absalom's poorest residents, at least in the past, as he had lived in The Puddles but rose to prominence after his insightful contributions during the Black Echelon Uprising.

locations.name: Eternal Shackle
locations.summary: The Eternal Shackle is a 20-foot-tall stone arch monument at the northernmost edge of Misery Row in Absalom. A massive magic flame burned beneath the arch. Locals say that the flame did not burn for decades until the Flesh Taxes were reinstated in 4635 AR, legalizing slavery once more.

locations.name: Evergreen Park
locations.summary: Evergreen Park, located in the Eastgate district, is the city's largest park, maintaining a perpetual spring thanks to the efforts of the Children of Spring, a Gozreh cult led by Lady Evigail of House Wycomb.

locations.name: FIARA
locations.summary: FIARA is a clothing store in the Grand Bazaar run by the mysterious and eponymous FIARA. The designs she creates are as strange as her past, which she speaks of in riddles that suggest she has escaped some kind of catastrophe, but no one knows exactly where she came from.

locations.name: Fall's End
locations.summary: Fall's End is a neighborhood beneath Absalom, a mile deep, with an underground lake formed by the flooded sewer system of The Puddles. Refugees, criminals, drug addicts, and Norgorber cultists inhabit the area, and one can encounter the most diverse mix of people imaginable here.

locations.name: Fallen Fortress
locations.summary: The Fallen Fortress is one of the many siege castles that attacked Absalom, proving impenetrable even to the legendary pathfinder Durvin Gest. During an earthquake, the Grasping Tower, as this structure was known, suffered damage, causing its eastern wing to collapse and allowing access to the structure—something that...

locations.name: Father's Forge
locations.summary: The Father's Forge is a temple dedicated to Torag in Westgate, whose modest size might cause confusion given that it is the predominant faith of the city's sizable dwarven minority.

locations.name: Fenworth Gameporium
locations.summary: Fenworth Gameporium is a card and deck factory that creates, locates, and distributes various games throughout the city, being popular among the casinos and nobles of Absalom who are always looking for new forms of entertainment.

locations.name: Fiddlemourn Manor
locations.summary: Fiddlemourn Manor is a private estate in Absalom's Petal District. It is owned by Oved Blakros, the maternal cousin of Michellia Blakros, first daughter of the Blakros family. Oved spends most of the year in the Taldan city of Cassomir attending to family business, which leaves Fiddlemourn unoccupied most of the time.

locations.name: Fierce Stripe
locations.summary: The Fierce Stripe is a shop where all of Absalom's badger needs are met. Lady Chesne of House Yuriel runs the shop, acquiring unique breeds of badgers for adoption by the residents of Westgate, where the animal has supplanted dogs and cats as a pet.

locations.name: Five-Fire Pavilions
locations.summary: The Five-Fire Pavilions is a burnt-out structure with exposed blackened metal beams that can be considered Absalom's goblin embassy, ​​led by the explorer Skirma Toadlicker, who seeks to show that goblins are ready to join the "civilized" world.

locations.name: Flint Tower
locations.summary: Flint Tower is one of the many siege castles that attacked Absalom. It has remained in good condition and has been used as a laboratory for alchemist and herbalist research throughout the ages. Its last resident was the pathfinder Andrax d'Aponte, who used the interior laboratories for his purposes.

locations.name: Flotsam Graveyard
locations.summary: The Flotsam Graveyard is a large field of shipwrecks that poses a hazard to shipping through Absalom Harbor, but serves to protect the southern portion of the city from foreign navies.

locations.name: Flower Street Market
locations.summary: The Flower Street Market, which runs alongside Ivy District Park, is full of flowering trees and bustling activity. It's a wide street where carts and carriages can pass side by side, and it connects to the Wise Quarter to the north.

locations.name: Flying Alderman
locations.summary: The Flying Alderman is a modest inn on the edge of the Foreign Quarter, serving as a safe house for Pathfinder Society agents. Drock Ovix, the innkeeper, is a Pathfinder himself and allows them to use tunnels beneath the inn that connect directly to the Grand Lodge—a closely guarded secret of the organization.

locations.name: Forae Logos
locations.summary: Also known as the Wise House and Library of Kortos, the Forae Logos in Absalom's Wise Quarter is the city's oldest and largest library, and one of the most extensive archives of written texts west of the Pit of Gormuz.

locations.name: Foreign Quarter Council Hall
locations.summary: The Foreign Quarter Council Hall is where the district's council meets, and Diplomatic Minister Ferridan Severus also maintains several offices there that are assigned to foreign diplomats for their meetings or other tasks when within the city's grounds.

locations.name: Fort Tempest
locations.summary: Fort Tempest is a stronghold built near the Puddles district in Absalom within the Flotsam Graveyard. A family of dwarves built the fortress from the remains of a previous siege tower that Kharnas the Angel-Binder constructed during the Radiant Siege in 1619 AR.

locations.name: Free Union Headquarters
locations.summary: The Free Union Headquarters is located in The Coins, a beautiful three-story building created by the freed slaves who make up the organization. Milly Tundall, the organization's director, has her office inside, although she is rarely at her desk, preferring to go outside.

locations.name: Gallery Rousa
locations.summary: Gallery Rousa is a popular and controversial art gallery in the Wise Quarter whose exhibitions change regularly and whose subject matter is criticized for its provocative nature.

locations.name: Gallery of Innovation
locations.summary: The Gallery of Innovation is the Brigh temple in Absalom run by the impassive High Priestess Flindish Tanwhirl. Followers from all over the Inner Sea come to the temple, which is filled with engineers, blacksmiths, and metalworkers who push their skills to the limit working in the workshops inside.

locations.name: Gerig's Workshop
locations.summary: Gerig's Workshop is where the popular drink of Gerig the Inspirer is produced, and since its production is a trade secret, there are always many Guild of Spears guards patrolling the area.

locations.name: Gillmen Tunnels
locations.summary: The Gillmen Tunnels are used by the azarketi community of Gilltown to avoid traveling overland to the city bay. These tunnels are submerged and therefore only easily navigable by aquatic creatures, making them a poorly monitored smuggling route into the city.

locations.name: Gilltown
locations.summary: Gilltown is a secluded collection of crude surface buildings in southern Eastgate, a district of Absalom, where azarketi ply their public trades. The surface neighborhood is a facade for an underground and underwater tunnel community leading to the Bay of Kortos.

locations.name: Girma's Games Galore!
locations.summary: Girma's Games Galore! is a stall that uses an extradimensional portal to create a gambling hall with a wide variety of games. Girma Nomer and her two sisters don't pay taxes or licenses, not because they can't afford it, but because it's more exciting to have to move at the slightest sound of a guard.

locations.name: Goblin King's Court
locations.summary: The Goblin King's Court is a series of wooden walkways and towers resembling a castle amidst the flooded houses of The Puddles. It is where Zusgut resides, acting as king. The goblins' short stature makes them reluctant to walk through the wet streets, so they hop from house to house to reach the court.

locations.name: God's Market
locations.summary: This street in Absalom's Ascendant Court houses a market where many of the city's religions sell religious items such as religious symbols, water, texts, and clothing. Scrolls, potions, and other minor magic items, as well as the services of moneylenders and skilled craftsmen such as jewelers, are also available.

locations.name: Golden Serpent
locations.summary: The Golden Serpent is a restaurant in the Ivy District run by Sendeli Foxglove, one of the newly arrived nobles in the city. The establishment is housed in a historic building with high ceilings and marble columns that had previously held several failed businesses and was believed to be cursed, until the restaurant's s...

locations.name: Gorumarrux
locations.summary: The Gorumarrux is a temple of Gorum and combat venue in Absalom's Ascendant Court. Its arena master and high priest of Gorum is Jaruke Dalagander, and as of 4720 AR Ledford was its undefeated champion. The fate of the Gorumarrux after the death of Gorum in 4724 AR is unknown.

locations.name: Grand Bazaar
locations.summary: For other meanings of "Grand Bazaar", please see Grand Bazaar (disambiguation). Nearly anything can be found for sale in the Grand Bazaar of The Coins district in Absalom. The area has few permanent buildings, and most goods are sold from tents, carts, portable stages, and merchant wagons.

locations.name: Grand Council Hall
locations.summary: The Grand Council Hall is a magnificent, large white marble structure where the city's most influential people meet to discuss the city's laws and administration.

locations.name: Grand Dance Hall of Kortos
locations.summary: The Grand Dance Hall of Kortos is an ornate, round theater on the district of The Coins in the city of Absalom. The city's richest merchants and most ambitious nobles gather in the theater to organise deals in order to control the economy of the Inner Sea.

locations.name: Grand Holt
locations.summary: The Grand Holt is a massive, multi-trunked fig tree located in the Green Ridge neighborhood of Absalom's Eastgate district. It is the oldest and largest tree on the Isle of Kortos, maybe even older than Absalom.

locations.name: Grand Lodge
locations.summary: For another meaning of "Grand Lodge", please see Grand Lodge (faction). The Grand Lodge is the world headquarters for the organization of explorers known as the Pathfinder Society. Located in the Foreign Quarter of the city of Absalom, it is a massive fortress surrounded by tall stone walls.

locations.name: Grand Vault
locations.summary: The Grand Vault is an enormous hall within Azlanti Keep that serves as the final defense of the city of Absalom in case its walls and keeps are ever breached. The First Guard, Absalom's primary defense force, holds its assemblies in the room under the standards of the countless armies that have failed to breach the kee...

locations.name: Graveraker
locations.summary: This page contains spoilers for the following products: Agents of Edgewatch.You can disable this banner in your personal preferences. The Graveraker is an enormous excavation machine designed by Blune Bandersworth, using the Cane of the Maelstrom to power it and move such a heavy structure.

locations.name: Green Ridge
locations.summary: Green Ridge is a neighborhood in the Eastgate district of Absalom. It is one of smallest and least populated parts of the city. It contains a number of extensive gardens and parks, as well as several copses of trees scattered throughout it, that inspire the district's name.

locations.name: Greenstar Market
locations.summary: The Greenstar Market is an open-air market showcasing typical foods from the Lirgen and Yamasa populations, including live fish brought in barrels, and attracting a large local lizardfolk population.

locations.name: Greydog Manor
locations.summary: Greydog Manor stands opposite of the Ivy District Park, surrounded by six-foot-high stone walls topped with a wand and statues of hunting dogs that give the estate its name. Old ulfen Skelg lives within, his home filled with mementos of his homeland farther north.

locations.name: Grindylow's Goblet
locations.summary: The Grindylow's Goblet is a busy inn and tavern in the city of Escadar on the Isle of Erran. It is a large and well lit establishment, measuring 9,100 square feet, and is a popular entertainment venue for visitors to Escadar.

locations.name: Grislyfair
locations.summary: The Grislyfair is an attempted amusement park that the Grand Council created in the Precipice Quarter to attract new residents and generate jobs. Most of the performers would be wanderers, thus not exposed to the district's spiritual corruption, and the use of clockworks unafraid of spirits should ensure the park's smo...

locations.name: Grog Pit
locations.summary: The Grog Pit is the most notorious tavern and flophouse in the Docks district of Absalom. It is a dangerous place serving sour drinks. One third of the patrons are either cutpurses or con artists.

locations.name: Groggy Froggy
locations.summary: The Groggy Froggy is a Westgate tavern that changed hands when its previous owner was petrified by a gorgon in 4714 AR, and the tavern was passed on to Annara Laskin and the other staff members.

locations.name: Guiding Hand
locations.summary: The Guiding Hand is an establishment that offers food, shelter, and job opportunities in the poverty-stricken neighborhood of Mudhaven. Tern on the Wind is an elf from the Crown of the World who came to represent her insular people in the city, but upon witnessing the plight of the people in the streets, she began her...

locations.name: Guild of Wonders
locations.summary: The headquarters of the Guild of Wonders is ostensibly an unmarked, poorly received tourism attraction composed of creative taxidermy that purportedly depicts cryptids and other beings, and is located in a shoddy building in the Westgate neighborhood of Absalom.

locations.name: Gulgamodh
locations.summary: This page contains spoilers for the following products: Assault on Absalom.You can disable this banner in your personal preferences. Gulgamodh is a gargantuan construct that once stood guard over the Precipice Quarter of Absalom.

locations.name: Gutless Griffon
locations.summary: The Gutless Griffon is a tavern in the Ivy District that has become very popular thanks to its owner, Fronsac Shimm. He chooses the food and the music, but above all, it's his lively attitude that makes him so appealing. He introduces himself to new patrons by telling anecdotes or serving drinks.

locations.name: Hackamore House
locations.summary: Hackamore House is the leading carriage, harness, and tack store in Absalom, located in the Coins district. The business is run by the centaur Aetris Thunderhoof and her lover Glenair of House Jefreet, a druid born in Diobel.

locations.name: Hall of Commerce
locations.summary: The Hall of Commerce is a magnificent building, constructed in the most modern and ostentatious style, which serves as the government office of the Coin Council as well as a bank.

locations.name: Hall of Holies
locations.summary: The Hall of Holies is home to the Chamber of Ecclestials, the oldest district council in all Absalom and is even older than the Grand Council of Absalom. The Chamber of Ecclestials is made up of twenty members of prominent religions who meet within the hall once a month spending most of their time organizing and arrang...

locations.name: Hall of the Teriarch
locations.summary: The Hall of the Teriarch is a domed stronghold in central-east Diobel that is by far the tallest building in the town and serves as both the court and the offices for Lord Avid of House Arnsen.

locations.name: Hands-Off Healing
locations.summary: Hands-Off Healing is a stall that's a huge success thanks to the Ivy District's aristocracy. Imara Palinton sells magical potions and oils whose designs prevent the unpleasant aftertaste of many other potions, and the fact that these designs were stolen from another merchant hardly matters.

locations.name: Harpy's Gate
locations.summary: Harpy's Gate is in the middle of the half-finished eastern town wall of the town of Diobel. It is named for the creatures that plague the town and serves as a checkpoint for caravans.

locations.name: Hawkthorne's Shield
locations.summary: Hawkthorne's Shield is a heavily fortified tower in Absalom that also served as a vault for the most precious treasures of the former Chelaxian aristocrat Emilano Doreset. The tower is heavily protected by magical wards and guardians, including a pair of hulking iron golems.

locations.name: Healing Raft
locations.summary: { The Healing Raft is a boat that clerics from Sarenrae's House of Healing send floating to The Puddles to provide food and healing to its inhabitants. The priests navigate at low tide, inhaling the unbearable smell of those early morning hours, and the people are so desperate that within the first hour of their arriva...

locations.name: Hillview Station
locations.summary: Hillview Station is the Lotus Guard's base of operations and the Petal District courthouse, hosting the city's highest-profile trials. Inside, the galleries offer spacious viewing areas and elevated balconies for observing the proceedings, and the holding cells resemble luxury suites compared to other jails in the city...

locations.name: Historia Reliquary
locations.summary: The Historia Reliquary is a curio shop in the Grand Bazaar that resembles a museum, being a store covered by fabrics with displays of artifacts, sculptures, and books from different eras and places in Avistan.

locations.name: Hoag's Rickets and Rumples
locations.summary: Hoag's Rickets and Rumples is a posh, white, three-story, gaming house and inn in central Diobel that features spicy food, live bardic performances, and contests of skill and athletics.

locations.name: Hothouse
locations.summary: The Hothouse is the administrative headquarters of the Petal District, where the Conclave of Flowers meets. It also serves as a greenhouse, housing plants imported from around the world, symbolizing the transparency of the council's actions.

locations.name: House Uiry
locations.summary: House Uiry was an influential noble family in Absalom, like any other, playing the political game until 4673 AR. One night, a stranger was invited to the manor, and when the butler returned with the wine, he found the entire family dead, along with the staff.

locations.name: House of Guile
locations.summary: The House of Guile is a gallery in Eastgate where Parsin Guile exhibits his works—some artistic, others more practical, featuring mechanical designs in wood—to the general public. The commercial side is managed by his wife, Hilenda Guile.

locations.name: House of Healing
locations.summary: The House of Healing is a Sarenite temple in the Ivy District in Absalom. It offers healing free of charge to any who need it and works to help former slaves in the city. As of 4720 AR, Zharichela was the House's high priestess.

locations.name: House of Seven Faces
locations.summary: The House of Seven Faces is a Westgate temple dedicated to Desna where her followers can rest. The clergy dislike ostentatious cathedrals, so there is little decoration except for the seven faces that appeared on the facade the first night the temple was built, and whose origin remains a mystery.

locations.name: House of Shade and Grace
locations.summary: The House of Shade and Grace is a popular Thuvian-style inn in the Foreign Quarter of the city. Built of sun-dried brick, it serves food that evokes memories of home for its guests.

locations.name: House of the Cresting Wave
locations.summary: The House of the Cresting Wave is the only known embassy of the amphibious humanoids known as the azarketi or gillmen above the waves, and is located in the town of Escadar in the domain of Absalom.

locations.name: Humbolt's Outfitters
locations.summary: Humbolt's Outfitters is a general store run by the merchant Gron Humbolt in The Coins and thanks to his wife, Lady Myleena, it has gained a great reputation in recent years.

locations.name: Hunting Lodge Seven
locations.summary: Hunting Lodge Seven is one of the hundreds of lodges in the city of Absalom, most of which were abandoned over time. Located between The Docks and the Foreign Quarter, it is considered neutral territory, used by the guard to hold prisoners when resolving jurisdictional issues.

locations.name: Irorium
locations.summary: The Irorium is an enormous open-air coliseum located in Absalom's Foreign Quarter that showcases non-lethal gladiatorial combat, mock sea-battles, religious festivals, and many other types of events and is the largest arena in the Inner Sea region.

locations.name: It Sparkles!
locations.summary: It Sparkles! is an Ivy District jewelry store run by the gnome Jembar Duskyshankle, primarily catering to the nobility who have arrived in Absalom in recent years. The store's popularity takes a hit due to its owner's abrasive and rude attitude.

locations.name: Ivy District Park
locations.summary: The Ivy District Park occupies a significant portion of the district, offering wonderful flora and fauna cared for by the leshy community and the druids of the Perfumer's Conglomerate. Stone bridges cross the park's ponds, home to owls, squirrels, fish, frogs, and ducks.

locations.name: Ivy Playhouse
locations.summary: The Ivy Playhouse is at the heart of Absalom, both physically and metaphysically, as the finest works from all of Golarion are presented daily in the theater, which changes with the seasons.

locations.name: Javelin Gallery
locations.summary: The Javelin Gallery is the base of operations for the Guild of Spears, composed of veteran guards who have joined as mercenaries. The structure was a second-millennium manor house converted into a defensive fortification and boasts enough forges to equip an entire army if needed.

locations.name: Josie's Kennel
locations.summary: Josie's Kennel is a pet shop located in the Grand Bazaar, run by the friendly retired clerk Josie. The shop has all kinds of pets, many of them abandoned around the city and looking for a new home.

locations.name: Kaldroon's Smokehouse
locations.summary: Kaldroon's Smokehouse is a rustic oceanside seafood restaurant in west-central Diobel run by Jitsy Kaldroon. It offers cheap and tasty crab and smoked oysters—popular with both commoners and wealthy merchants, as well as out-of-towner. Customers are often told to expect long lines.

locations.name: Kennel (Absalom)
locations.summary: The Kennel appears to be an unremarkable taxidermy shop, in a state of disrepair similar to other buildings in the district, but it's used by the Family Dogs criminal gang, named for all the taxidermied dogs found in the establishment's basement.

locations.name: Kin Gate
locations.summary: The Kin Gate is located in the northeast of Absalom. It was originally a siege castle, commissioned by the fey prince Juroveal during the Siege of Kin, but when he was banished, the fortification was merged with the rest of the city.

locations.name: Kitten's Slumber
locations.summary: Kitten's Slumber is a shop that appears to be run by Roswine Yarindam, a dwarf, but everyone knows that her familiar, Cabbage, is the one really in charge. This shop takes in the familiars of deceased spellcasters, caring for them and finding them new companions.

locations.name: Knight Country
locations.summary: The upper reaches of Azlanti Keep in Absalom are known as Knight Country, since it is the domain of siege engineers, specialists, and senior members of the First Guard, and requires a badge for entry. The rooms are expansive and well-decorated, although windows and balconies are reserved for siege equipment.

locations.name: Knitty Gritty
locations.summary: Knitty Gritty is a shop in the Grand Bazaar run by three catfolk sisters, the eldest being Tarissa. They sell knitted products such as scarves and sweaters, popular in the autumn and winter seasons.

locations.name: Kortos Watercrafts
locations.summary: The Kortos Watercrafts is a shipyard that creates boats and small vessels using the finest quality wood on the island. They are owned by the Kortos Consortium, which uses the vessels to navigate the region's waterways.

locations.name: Kraken's Ink Tattoo
locations.summary: The Kraken's Ink Tattoo is a tattoo shop in the Grand Bazaar whose design is reminiscent of the style of shops more commonly found in The Docks. Arhan Benimaya displays several of his tattoos on his arms and keeps his dog nearby to calm his emotions when he gets frustrated while working.

locations.name: Kyonin Embassy
locations.summary: The Kyonin Embassy is located in the Ivy District, a gathering place for artists and a haven for the free-spirited elves of the forest nation. The manor house is built in the Castrovel style, and a number of ambassadors are rotating through, pursuing the nation's goals in Absalom.

locations.name: Labyrinth of Absalom
locations.summary: The Labyrinth of Absalom is the place where, according to the stories, Aroden fought a creature that had been brought forth when he raised the Isle of Kortos. Although the nature of the monster changes depending on the storyteller, what remains constant is that it continues to live in the volcanic caverns beneath the s...

locations.name: Lair of the Crownsworn
locations.summary: The Lair of the Crownsworn is located in a series of ancient chambers beneath their shop, Crystal Creations. Those in the know can set aside a display case and descend a spiral staircase into this thieves' base of operations.

locations.name: Lantern Lodge
locations.summary: For other meanings of "Lantern Lodge", please see Lantern Lodge (disambiguation). After being purchased by Venture-Captain Amara Li for a large sum of money, the Lantern Lodge in the Petal District of Absalom reflects the finest culture that the city has to offer.

locations.name: Laughing Sword
locations.summary: The Laughing Sword is a tidy magic item shop in Absalom's Ivy District. Its owner is Peren Ambergross, a slender gnome with sea-green hair and an assortment of cheap but tidy three-piece suits.

locations.name: Learned Pig
locations.summary: The Learned Pig is one of the most popular taverns in the Wise Quarter. It doesn't follow the trend of affiliating with any single educational institution, preferring to remain neutral and welcoming students from all walks of life to sample its strong drinks.

locations.name: Liferoot Stone
locations.summary: The Liferoot Stone is one of the aeon towers that Aroden placed around the Isle of Kortos. The tower was a 300-foot-tall mudbrick step pyramid with a flat 10-foot-wide top and four uneven tiers, though it is now partially collapsed.

locations.name: Lifter's Mooring
locations.summary: Lifter's Mooring is a dockworkers' union led by Guyton Grerton, who is considered an idol and symbol of the city's workers. The union deals with businesses by offering contracts that meet the needs of their employers and ensuring the rights of their workers.

locations.name: Lions' Square
locations.summary: The Lions' Square is located in the Foreign Quarter and is one of the largest enclaves in the district where Taldor expatriates can live in peace. After every war, famine, and political conflict, the district receives new migrants, and with the prohibition of faith in Sarenrae by Stavian I, many of the inhabitants are...

locations.name: Little Inner Sea
locations.summary: Little Inner Sea is a neighborhood in The Puddles where members of the Salvage Guild meet in a completely flooded area. It was once a public park, but the saltwater hasn't been kind to the trees.

locations.name: Little Lirgen
locations.summary: Little Lirgen is a neighborhood in the Foreign Quarter where the diaspora of the fallen nation of Lirgen gathers, and most of them maintain their nation's astronomical traditions.

locations.name: Little Roofs
locations.summary: The roofs of buildings in the southern part of Azlanti Keep in Absalom, although flat and accessible to siege equipment, are not manned. The area serves as a meeting place for off-duty members of the First Guard.

locations.name: Lost & Found
locations.summary: Lost & Found is an unassuming trinket shop in the Grand Bazaar, run by the dwarf Yggwil. Many avoid it, preferring more eye-catching shops, but it's a place where pathfinders, treasure hunters, and mercenaries gather, as every now and then an object with wondrous powers appears on its shelves.

locations.name: Lucky Nimbus
locations.summary: The Lucky Nimbus is one of Absalom's most prestigious casinos, located in The Coins, where all the city's money converges. This establishment is known for its high security and discerning clientele.

locations.name: Lyrics on the Wind
locations.summary: Lyrics on the Wind is a stall in the Grand Bazaar that sells lyrics, poems, and songs customized by the artist Thelba Griddlestrum. She runs this stall because of a scandal that banished her from interacting with the city's high society.

locations.name: Madinani Manor
locations.summary: The Madinani Manor is an imposing estate with a white wall, gardens with plants used for arcane or alchemical purposes, and a three-story building in the center. This impressive structure serves as the home of Lady Darchana, one of Absalom's most prominent political figures and a master of arcane magic.

locations.name: Magpie Manor
locations.summary: Magpie Manor is located in the Petal District and serves as a social club and retirement home where the city's most famous actors, explorers, and artisans can relax with each other's company.

locations.name: Mama Shrog's Solutions
locations.summary: Mama Shrog's Solutions is a shop that was bought years ago by a woman called Mama Shrog. The building has a grotesque history, having belonged to a painter who murdered his entire family to obtain the specific colour of red he sought.

locations.name: Margruel's Masts
locations.summary: Margruel's Masts is a popular shipyard in The Docks, building cutters and caravels that serve a variety of purposes for both sailors and merchants.

locations.name: Material Changes
locations.summary: Material Changes is a boutique that offers appearance alterations using a combination of counterfeit products with transmutation and illusion magic. The owner, Mistress Iltara Clavela, offers minor changes, usually for those who want to look younger, as well as radical transformations that leave even friends and family...

locations.name: Meilin and Zhen Ships
locations.summary: Meilin and Zhen Ships is a shipyard run by natives of Tian Xia who repair ships after long ocean voyages, such as those departing from or arriving from Goka. They build ships in the style of their continent, as these remain popular with the city's nobility.

locations.name: Menhemes Manor (Absalom)
locations.summary: The Menhemes Manor stands against the wall facing Absalom in Westgate, the home of one of the city's oldest noble families. House Menhemes has constructed several black pyramids, a corridor lined with sphinx statues, and sand gardens that showcase their lineage to the nation of Osirion, but what is most striking is the...

locations.name: Mercerene Manor
locations.summary: Mercerene Manor is the residence of House Mercerene, boasting extensive courtyards and gardens, and is where the retired Pathfinder Haimon Heuff resides. Adventurers of all kinds visit the manor, captivating its old lord with passionate tales of adventure that evoke memories of bygone days.

locations.name: Merrygleam
locations.summary: Merrygleam offers toys that delight both adults and children, people in need of joy in their lives. It's a colorful shop run by Ozi and her sisters, and also serves as a shrine to Picoperi.

locations.name: Metringer Sanitarium
locations.summary: Metringer Sanitarium has been in operation since 4000 AR, serving as a place of healing and medicine for those suffering from mental illness, as well as a site for ethically questionable experiments on these patients.

locations.name: Metro-Cathedral
locations.summary: The Metro-Cathedral is a church in Abadar, The Puddles, where the organ, which survived the earthquake of 4698 AR, is played every Oathday. The same cannot be said of one of its towers, which collapsed and crushed seven people.

locations.name: Misery Row
locations.summary: Misery Row is a street running along the eastern edge of the Coins district of Absalom, and was until recently was the only street in the city where the slave trade was always legal. Slavery was abolished in Absalom following the events of the Fiendflesh Siege of 4717 AR.

locations.name: Mithril Chef
locations.summary: The Mithril Chef is a high-end restaurant that also serves as a second-mark Firebrands cell located in The Docks district. All its staff are members of the organization, led by Claudette Butterfoot, who is more focused on cooking than going on adventures, though she frequently gives her employees "vacations", after whi...

locations.name: Mithril Hall
locations.summary: The Mithril Hall is a beautiful, traditional-style structure in Westgate that serves as offices and residences for the bureaucrats and diplomats of the Western Council, which administers the district.

locations.name: Mohren's Mobility Apparel
locations.summary: Mohren's Mobility Apparel looks more like a warehouse more than a shop, but inside one can smell burning incense and hear the sounds of the owner, Morhen, creating a new prosthesis.

locations.name: Monger's Mart
locations.summary: The Monger's Mart is a cheap open market in the Coins district of Absalom where poor quality goods are sold. Spoiled cheeses, meats, and especially spices that have lost their value are sold in huge tents by sellers from all over the world.

locations.name: Morilla Palace and the Tally Wall
locations.summary: Morilla Palace is a beautiful residence with magnificent gardens, incredible paintings and sculptures, and traps everywhere, capable of killing in ways one can't even imagine.

locations.name: Mortecant
locations.summary: Mortecant is a neighborhood in the southern part of the Precipice Quarter where followers of Urgathoa, seeking to be corrupted by the area's necromantic energies, move from abandoned house to abandoned house, weaving through a tangled web of people as if they were undead.

locations.name: Mother Sphinx
locations.summary: Mother Sphinx is a shop a few blocks from the Grand Bazaar where Horner Shan sells household gadgets at great prices. Behind secret doors, illusions, and traps in the underground lies a temple dedicated to Norgorber, where Horner is its high priest, praying to the Gray Master aspect of the deity.

locations.name: Mudhaven
locations.summary: Mudhaven is a small region located in the southwestern corner of the Coins district in the city of Absalom.

locations.name: Mystic Sweets and Other Treats
locations.summary: Mystic Sweets and Other Treats is a potion shop whose potions, unlike traditional bitter ones, feature fruit and mint flavors thanks to the alchemist Roxley Remire.

locations.name: Nature's Bearings
locations.summary: Nature's Bearings is a shop that sells natural products, from flowers to paints, bringing a touch of nature to the accustomed urban life of Absalom. The shop is run by Adelyn Montara, whose mother was a druid, and she is helped by her mother's bear, which has grown intelligent and learned to paint.

locations.name: No Left Feet
locations.summary: No Left Feet is a stall where one can always see someone moving and music playing, because it's here that Jacinato teaches dance steps to musicians and dancers from Absalom.

locations.name: Northman's Woodworks Galleria
locations.summary: Northman's Woodworks Galleria is a shop run by the busy Hans the Northman, one of the best, if not the best, woodworker in all of Absalom. Orders can be placed at the entrance, or you can pay a fee to walk around the workshop, as there is also a gallery of great interest to those with a passion for woodworking.

locations.name: Noses That Know
locations.summary: Noses That Know is a perfume shop run by the pixie couple Merin and Kolbe of Absalom. They have traveled the world and their keen sense of smell allows them to know which perfumes suit each customer, although they often sell perfumes with the scents of foods they love.

locations.name: Ogrekin Hall
locations.summary: For other meanings of "Ogrekin", please see Ogrekin (disambiguation). Ogrekin is a transporting business located in the Docks district of Absalom. Ogrekin can move anything that needs moving anywhere within the city.

locations.name: Open Quartering
locations.summary: The Open Quartering, known as the Open, is a large military and guard market within Azlanti Keep in Absalom. The quartermaster, Lord Yuvin Vatir of House Damaq, and his rasars sell goods at low, reasonable prices to members of the First Guard or district guards.

locations.name: Opparan Trade Commission
locations.summary: The Opparan Trade Commission is a guildhall established in 4714 AR for the purpose of carrying out commissions that benefit everyone, though a little more for Taldor wouldn't hurt. Merchants of the nation and nobles such as House Morilla, House Madinani, and House Tsoulet are especially associated with the commission.

locations.name: Outer Gate
locations.summary: The Outer Gate, which runs through Azlanti Keep, is the largest gate in Absalom and possibly even the world. It stands 200 feet high, 100 feet wide, and 20 feet thick, and is equipped with internal guard positions and balconies that allow the guards to fire straight down.

locations.name: Palace Ormuz
locations.summary: The Palace Ormuz is a white Thuvian-style structure where Scion Lord Yamthar invites the aristocracy to seminars where they can speak with researchers, scholars, and intellectuals, listening to or testing their theories.

locations.name: Palace of Thirteen Spires
locations.summary: The Palace of Thirteen Spires is a small but opulent palace in the Wise Quarter, divided into four wings, each in a Chelaxian, Osirian, Taldan, and Minkan style. For most of the year, the rooms are rented to merchants and nobles visiting the city.

locations.name: Parties in Parcels
locations.summary: Parties in Parcels is a store that sells party supplies like confetti, ribbons, and fireworks, and while these are popular, the most eye-catching item is the "party in a box".

locations.name: Pasharran's Domain
locations.summary: Pasharran's Domain is located in the catacombs where the Ivy District, Wise Quarter, and Ascendant Court intersect. He only emerges to the surface once a month to meet with Aarnock Xanthiss, with whom he trades potions and magic. The old lich is a fervent follower of Urgathoa, and his home reeks of death and decay.

locations.name: Penny & Sphinx Trust
locations.summary: The Penny & Sphinx Trust is a bank in The Coins, run mostly by halflings. It's a large stone building surrounded by a lawn, enclosed by a gate and iron fences, flanked by two pairs of sphinxes. In 4720 AR, they had trouble with robbers, culminating in a failed heist by the Copper Hand.

locations.name: Pickled Imp
locations.summary: The Pickled Imp is a curio shop in The Docks run by the infamous Guaril Karela, though he's rarely seen there. It now operates more like a pawn shop, keeping no records of any transactions, making it impossible to know what's being sold, bought, or who the customers are.

locations.name: Pig's Paunch
locations.summary: The Pig's Paunch is a tavern in The Coins district of Absalom. The Pig's Paunch was one of the bars at which the Pathfinder Society was founded on 23 Desnus, 4307 AR, and at one point had been a subject of dispute over the Society's founding.

locations.name: Pikapell Market
locations.summary: Pikapell Market is the largest market within the Bristles District of Diobel. Even locals disagree whether the name hails from cries of "Pick a pearl!" or "Pick a pelt!" and agruments over this has led to the odd drunken brawl.

locations.name: Pilot Island
locations.summary: Pilot Island is located at the center of the Flotsam Graveyard of Absalom. It houses the Absalom Lighthouse, Pilot House, and Harbormaster's Grange. The Starwatch has jurisdiction for law enforcement on this island even though it is technically outside of the actual city of Absalom.

locations.name: Pitview Pub
locations.summary: Pitview Pub in the Ascendant Court is a tavern where people can go to bet on which aspirant has the best chance of entering the Starstone Cathedral. It has a cellar with windows overlooking the cliff where patrons can watch the aspirants plummet to their deaths after jumping.

locations.name: Places To Go
locations.summary: Places To Go is a cart pushed by the dwarf Gromli Tullman in the back alleys of the Grand Bazaar. Dozens of scrolls and maps fill the cart, and Gromli has an unusual way of selling them: he goes out to find a customer and offers them the chance to buy a map, saying that following it led them to interesting places.

locations.name: Pleasure Salon of Calistria
locations.summary: Elves and aiuvarins are common among the temple prostitutes of the Pleasure Salon of Calistria in the Ascendant Court district of Absalom. Elves are otherwise relatively uncommon in Absalom, mostly consisting of adventurers or outcasts; more common are their half-elven descendants.

locations.name: Postern
locations.summary: The Postern Gate, or simply the Postern, is the eastern gate of Absalom. It is the smallest of the city's gates, only 50 feet high and 40 feet wide, and the only one that is normally kept closed and locked.

locations.name: Pride of Azir
locations.summary: The Pride of Azir is an efficient shipyard in Absalom, focusing on creating dhows and with Rahadoum's considerable influence on its affairs.

locations.name: Primarch's Residence
locations.summary: The Primarch's Residence is surrounded by high stone walls and enormous gardens, possibly the most extensive in the city. It is in this majestic building that the Primarch should reside, though since Lord Gyr's disappearance, the building has fallen into disuse.

locations.name: Princely Shipyard
locations.summary: The Princely Shipyard produces barques and schooners in a medium-sized warehouse. Its owners are loyal to the Taldan-based House Madinani and support Lady Darchana.

locations.name: Prophet's Academy
locations.summary: Prophet's Academy is a vast manor house in the north-east of the Coins district of Absalom, purchased by Trevlin Crest and Ilrava Drogand, two followers of the Prophecies of Kalistrade who came to Absalom from Kerse to acquire the city's great riches.

locations.name: Protectorate Anthology
locations.summary: The Protectorate Anthology is where the Learned Guard operates, patrolling the Wise Quarter and they are located on the stairs leading to the Forae Logos which they defend with fervor.

locations.name: Purewater Home
locations.summary: The Purewater Home is an orphanage that takes in the most unfortunate children in The Puddles while also serving as the base of operations for the local Firebrands cell, run by Hope, the building's owner.

locations.name: Pyramid of the Dog
locations.summary: The Pyramid of the Dog is a siege castle located on the beach south of the town of Shoreline near Absalom, with easy access to the city's Puddles district. It is one of the closest siege castles to Absalom's walls. Three battered, ancient towers have collapsed inward toward the fourth, forming a huge wreck.

locations.name: Rat-Taker's Palace
locations.summary: The Rat-Taker's Palace is the base of operations for the city's cleaners, responsible for maintaining the sewers, repairing pipes, and pest control. The building was abandoned after the earthquake, but they quickly returned to reclaim it, as its ostentatious appearance was too tempting to not move back in.

locations.name: Ravounel Consulate
locations.summary: The Ravounel Consulate is the embassy of the free nation of Ravounel, established in 4717 AR by Ambassador Vita Aulamaxa to promote relations and represent its interests in a city as important as Absalom.

locations.name: Razorhall
locations.summary: Razorhall is a temple dedicated to the murderous aspect of Norgorber known as Father Skinsaw. The building, the former district courthouse, lies amidst the flooded houses of The Puddles. The cultists now hold sham trials where the accused are always found guilty and subjected to gruesome and creative executions.

locations.name: Re:Freshments
locations.summary: Re:Freshments is a café in the Grand Bazaar run by Dilyn Willers, offering mixed drinks, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic.
