What makes the establishment stand out from the competition is the use of alchemy in the drinks, which produce non-dangerous but curious effects on the customers who consume them.

locations.name: Reclaimed Paradise
locations.summary: Reclaimed Paradise looks more like a spa than a vehicle repair shop, with a garden featuring palm trees and a 14-foot-high gray wall surrounding a simple shop. Inside, Clemeth Falk works daily, meticulously repairing vehicles with a staff that provides excellent customer service.

locations.name: Red Bridge
locations.summary: Red Bridge crosses the Deluge River, connecting Diobel, and since the town's founding, a local market has been located in the area, selling goods from this elevated position. Wizard duels were also popular near the bridge, but when they ended up destroying the stalls and their owners, they were outlawed by Lord Avid.

locations.name: Red Bridge Pearl Market
locations.summary: The Red Bridge Pearl Market is the favoured place for pearl vendors and wizard duels in the Absalomian town of Diobel. This is despite the fact the magical duels recently having acquired prohibited status. It is located both on and under the Red Bridge that crosses the Deluge River.

locations.name: Red Drake Warehouses
locations.summary: Red Drake Warehouses is a series of warehouses in The Docks run by Ptarnex Dexarion, the ruthless boss of Ogrekin Hall. He runs the business by offering merchants space to store whatever they want, with the caveat that if they fail to pay for even a single month, all the merchandise inside becomes his property.

locations.name: Red Redoubt
locations.summary: Karamoss the Machine Mage began assaulting Absalom in 3637 AR in order to gain control of the Starstone. To wage his siege, he constructed a huge metal, clockwork citadel in a single night that rose from the rocky ground like a red metallic growth.

locations.name: Red Silk Route
locations.summary: The Red Silk Route is a region of the Grand Bazaar in the Coins district of Absalom that is cordoned off with red silk flags for the sale of hedonistic goods and services, opiate drugs, and explicit shows. Both the Token Guard and the Forthright maintain security in this area.

locations.name: Relics & Remembrance
locations.summary: Relics & Remembrance is a simple-looking shop in the Grand Bazaar that houses a collection of stories written by the owner, Khisa. Customers can sip tea while reading a book, and all the stories are about travelers she has met, though some are a bit exaggerated.

locations.name: Restful Pathfinders' Lounge
locations.summary: The Restful Pathfinders' Lounge is located in the Petal District of Absalom. Established several decades ago by several affluent Pathfinders, the lounge is a strictly members-only club intended as a temporary retreat from Pathfinder Society duties. The exclusive club is an ideal place for a relaxing smoke or drink.

locations.name: Rhet's Home
locations.summary: Rhet's Home is an orphanage in the northern part of Mudhaven. It appears to be an ordinary house, but the happy laughter of children playing in the yard can be heard.

locations.name: Ropecliffs
locations.summary: Ropecliffs is a neighborhood where smugglers from the Precipice Quarter gather, having taken up the trade to survive the calamity that befell the district. Through a system of pulleys attached to various abandoned buildings and the cliff itself, cargo can be hoisted from the sea to the city, though it's not very safe,...

locations.name: Salhar Estate
locations.summary: The Salhar Estate is where the Grand Ambassador of Osirion, Dremdhet Salhar, lives surrounded by walls and iron gates, with a personal guard patrolling the area to prevent intruders from entering.

locations.name: Sally Port
locations.summary: The Sally Port is the Sally Guard's base of operations and the gateway to the district, connecting it to Westerhold and Shoreline outside the city. The gate is specifically designed to facilitate cavalry charges, and tax collectors and bureaucrats record the trade passing through it, as the settlements of Otari, Galizh...

locations.name: Sanctum of Aroden
locations.summary: The Sanctum of Aroden, an underground site of Absalom's Church of Aroden whose location was kept a secret for millennia, served as a chapel and headquarters of the Arodenite monastic cult of the Order of the Aeon Star.

locations.name: Saucy Wench
locations.summary: The Saucy Wench meadhall is one of the very few of the permanent buildings in the Grand Bazaar in the Coins district of Absalom. The popular four-story edifice near the center of the bazaar serves roast meat, bread, and mead, and is well-known for its uniformed all-female waiting staff.

locations.name: Scabbit Camp
locations.summary: Scabbit Camp is located "in-land" to the east of the Absalomian town of Diobel. This encampment is populated by the quick to anger Scabbit family, including patriarch Makka Scabbits.

locations.name: Scales of Labor
locations.summary: The Scales of Labor was one of the slave pits on Misery Row and while not the most successful, it was the most typical, an example of what the others were like. This shop had cages and pits where slaves were kept, one pit housed those dedicated to pleasure, childcare, or those too old to cause trouble, while the others...

locations.name: School of Spells
locations.summary: The Pathfinder Society's School of Spells, part of its Grand Lodge in Absalom, trains Pathfinders in magical arts that include spellcasting, arcane lore, tactics, and the treatment of magical afflictions.

locations.name: School of the North Song-Wind
locations.summary: The School of the North Song-Wind, located in the Foreign Quarter, is a branch of the Magaambya. It consists of a grove of trees with fabric draped around the trunks, creating natural walls within the "structure".

locations.name: Scriveners' Square
locations.summary: Scriveners' Square is where the offices of most of the city's newspapers are located, publishing articles on politics, fashion, and entertainment for all who buy them.

locations.name: Sea King Shipyards
locations.summary: Sea King Shipyards is a small shipyard in the Docks district of the city of Absalom. The yard builds only one ocean-going vessel at a time, but it remains famous for the high quality and sturdiness of its fluyts and galleons that can sail the most dangerous waters in the Inner Sea.

locations.name: Seal of Kazutal
locations.summary: The Seal of Kazutal is a simple stone monument that serves as a shrine to the goddess in Absalom. Created by visitors from Arcadia while passing through, the monument has become a rallying point for freed slaves who are inspired by Kazutal's anti-slavery stance.

locations.name: Second Chance
locations.summary: Second Chance is a seedy bar in The Puddles with only one room and several exits. Fights break out all the time, and it's not uncommon to find one or two dead bodies on the floor each month.

locations.name: Second Labyrinth
locations.summary: The Second Labyrinth is a popular social and gambling club among chelaxians and gamblers in The Coins district, run by the beautiful Lady Azoria. The gothic exterior and gargoyles watching passersby are the first things one sees upon arrival, and inside, games of all kinds from Vudra to Riddleport fill the tables.

locations.name: Seventh Church of Iomedae
locations.summary: The Seventh Church of Iomedae is an important temple of goddess in the Ascendant Court district of Absalom, and the site of the seventh of Iomedae's 11 miraculous acts, the calling of the Undying Light.

locations.name: Sewer Dragon's Realm
locations.summary: The Sewer Dragon's Realm is located in a theater that sank into the earth in the Ivy District, where kobolds led by Yiddlepode gather to discuss their tasks. Although kobolds can be found throughout the underground, here the tunnels are protected by the deadly traps of Trapmaster Tok, and their damp, moldy nature disco...

locations.name: Shrine of Shelyn
locations.summary: The Shrine of Shelyn is situated in a flowering grove of the Ivy District Park, cared for by a clergy led by the artist Eleena Woodsong. The grove is filled with roses placed in locations of artistic significance, with swans swimming in the ponds and a single rose suspended in the air, changing color with each season.

locations.name: Shrine of the Failed
locations.summary: The Shrine of the Failed is a hall of monuments in Absalom's Ascendant Court to those who have failed the Test of the Starstone.

locations.name: Sianovel Agency
locations.summary: The Sianovel Agency is a consultancy and detective agency located in Erdan Sianovel's house in Westgate. It's sandwiched between a bakery and a woodworking shop, with an eye-catching window display.

locations.name: Silk Castle
locations.summary: The Silk Castle is a kite shop located in the Wise Quarter of Absalom. Its proprietor, Vittar Corusec, is often hired to judge special kite-fighting battles in the Irorium during the Gala of Sails and Kraken Carnival festivals held in spring and autumn respectively.

locations.name: Silken Court
locations.summary: The Silken Court is a brothel in the Petal District of Absalom. It is the city's most expensive establishment of its type, and among of the Inner Sea's most famous.

locations.name: Silkenhand
locations.summary: The Silkenhand is an Ivy District gang specializing in narcotics and sex work targeting the affluent members of the community. Unlike their rivals, the Crowsworn, they keep their clients' secrets behind closed doors.

locations.name: Siphons
locations.summary: The Siphons are a system of underground tunnels beneath the Absalom district of the Puddles. They consist of parts of the city's larger sewer system as well as an intricate series of crypts and emergency tunnels.

locations.name: Sirola Manor
locations.summary: Sirola Manor is a spacious building in Westgate, but not as ostentatious as some others in the city, being the residence of retired Pathfinder Venla and Urmas Sirola.

locations.name: Skinsaw Sanctum
locations.summary: The Skinsaw Sanctum is a series of rooms in the Catacombs that Wrent Discaspiron claimed and modeled to serve as the base for her macabre cult. It contains everything they need to carry out their horrific murders, including a place to create skin masks, a prayer room, and several rest rooms and spaces to practice bruta...

locations.name: Skyreach
locations.summary: The five-towered fortress of Skyreach, sometimes called Skyreach Tower, is the most prominent element of the Grand Lodge of Absalom's Pathfinder Society. Its central tower can be seen for miles around and is the meeting place of the Society's ruling council, the Decemvirate.

locations.name: Soggy Piper
locations.summary: The Soggy Piper is a tavern perched on a cliff in The Puddles, a hangout for criminals and cultists. Violent crime is commonplace there, as bodies can be disposed of by simply pushing them off the cliff into the sea.

locations.name: Sphinx Gate
locations.summary: The Sphinx Gate is located in the northwest of Absalom and is usually open even at night due to the constant traffic in the area. It connects to the farms of the region and is used by the First Guard to patrol the Cairnlands, taking its name from the enormous sphinx statue erected there.

locations.name: Spiral Shrine
locations.summary: The Spiral Shrine is a temple of Pharasma that was among the first to be rebuilt in the Precipice Quarter after the earthquake that shook the district. Hundreds of candles were placed in its alcoves to honor the memory of those whose bodies could not be recovered from the rubble, and the residents of Beldrin's Bluff do...

locations.name: Spiralcross Cemetery
locations.summary: The Spiralcross Cemetery is the largest and most prestigious cemetery in all of Absalom, where Primarch]s, nobles, and high priests are buried. Located next to the Ahnkamen Estate, this cemetery is a labyrinth of vaults and shrines belonging to families with over four millennia of history.

locations.name: Spire of Nex
locations.summary: The Spire of Nex, also called the Tower of Nex, is a tall siege castle created by the archmage Nex as part of his unsuccessful siege of Absalom in 166 AR. Nex constructed it using a shard from his personal demiplane known as the Crux of Nex.

locations.name: St. Sarnax monastery
locations.summary: St. Sarnax monastery was once a training academy and esoteric library located in the town of Escadar on Absalom's Isle of Erran. It is maintained by the remaining Knights of the Aeon Star—an ancient order of sword-mages whose members were Aroden's companions in the days before his ascension.

locations.name: Starspine Manor
locations.summary: Starspine Manor is a magnificent residence that would dwarf the surrounding houses were it not for its beautiful gardens. Lord Synarr Daidalos owns the manor, which appeared overnight between two adjacent residences, though this is only a rumor.

locations.name: Starstone Cathedral
locations.summary: Arguably the most sacred location in all of Golarion, the Starstone Cathedral is a monument to divinity. The massive structure was created by Aroden when he raised the Starstone from the depths of the Inner Sea in 1 AR, and the relic is believed to rest within to this day.

locations.name: Starstone Chasm
locations.summary: The Starstone Chasm surrounds the most important cathedral in the Inner Sea, its depth said to be infinite. However, the dwarves of Westerhold, in their efforts to excavate tunnels beneath the city, ended up opening holes in the surface of the chasm's walls.

locations.name: Starwatch Keep
locations.summary: The imposing Starwatch Keep is an enormous fortification perched on the cliffs overlooking Absalom Harbor with views of Pilot Island, the Flotsam Graveyard, and the city as a whole.

locations.name: Statue Street
locations.summary: Statue Street is a long stretch of road in the Absalom district of Westgate. Appropriately named, the street contains dozens of scattered statues in various poses. These are the remnants of an Absalom tradition that has only recently been outlawed.

locations.name: Statue of Primarch Harvi
locations.summary: The Statue of Primarch Harvi, located in the Petal District, is one of the city's most famous public artworks, but not for a positive reason as it's considered the most ugly statue in all of Absalom.

locations.name: Stilt House
locations.summary: The Stilt House is a city-owned building in the Puddles district of Absalom that serves as the headquarters of the district guard, the Muckruckers. It also serves as the headquarters of the Salvage Guild.

locations.name: Stinger's Scar
locations.summary: Stinger's Scar was a park called Celestial Pleasure Ground where the elite could spend their time enjoying its verdant gardens, but when an earthquake struck the city, a vermin infestation appeared out of nowhere.

locations.name: Stone Ring Pond
locations.summary: Stone Ring Pond is a small pond surrounded by landmark standing stones and situated on an overlook near Otari. The pond's waters are preternaturally still and reflective, and 24 age-weathered standing stones, each 12 feet high, surround it.

locations.name: Stoneshield House
locations.summary: Stoneshield House serves as the headquarters for the Graycloaks, the district watch of the Ascendant Court district of Absalom. Stoneshield House is named in honour of Dunarr Stoneshield, a former captain of the Graycloaks who is treated almost like a secular saint by serving members of the Graycloaks.

locations.name: Stormholt
locations.summary: Stormholt is a demiplane created by a coven of hags. Sunken ships from the Absalom nay are absorbed into the demiplane, along with their sailors, whose dreams are devoured by the hags, turning them into nightmares.

locations.name: Street Performers and Actors' Guild
locations.summary: The Street Performers and Actors' Guild was formed to capitalize on the popularity of entertainment and the talent that Absalom attracts, becoming the most successful guild in terms of its power to influence the future of people in the industry.

locations.name: Summit & Sundry
locations.summary: The Summit & Sundry offers worldly adventure luggage for adventurers of all kinds. The shop itself is a beautiful stone and wood building with vines and roses growing up the walls.

locations.name: Sundown Street
locations.summary: Sundown Street is a curving street near the city wall in the Ivy District, a few blocks from the bustling Flower Street Market. This street is renowned for housing the three most prestigious and sought-after tailors in all of Absalom: Ambroz Black, Al Amir Kai, and Madame Theodora Signe.

locations.name: Tallavont School
locations.summary: The Tallavont School was founded centuries ago by idealists seeking to foster a sense of community in Eastgate by creating an institution that would allow teachers persecuted in their home countries for their political beliefs to teach here instead of being entangled in the city's treacherous and infighting politics.

locations.name: Taurean Embassy
locations.summary: The Taurean Embassy is a residence built in the style of Iblydos, and it's where one of Absalom's most curious inhabitants, the albino minotaur Nuar Spiritskin, lives. He was banished by his tribe from the Kortos Mounts, and being just over seven feet tall, he had no trouble integrating into human society.

locations.name: Tempering Hall
locations.summary: The Tempering Hall is a combat school located across the main street from the Seventh Church in the Ascendant Court district of Absalom. The facility traditionally trains paladins of Iomedae as well as those called by Abadar, Irori, and Shelyn, a few of whom supplement the dozens of paladins of Iomedae trained by the e...

locations.name: Tempest
locations.summary: Tempest is a nightclub in the Ivy District that was formerly a theater with a second floor containing apartments. Thanks to the illusions employed by the establishment, an esoteric and incomprehensible aesthetic is revealed, even though the common man is not permitted entry if they were the establishment would make no...

locations.name: Temple Row
locations.summary: Temple Row is a neighborhood teeming with temples to various deities, most of them related to the sea and weather, located in The Docks. The temple of Gozreh is near tide pools that fluctuate with the high ot low tide, generating a good amount of wind, and the area is favored by water druids.

locations.name: Temple of Lost Coins
locations.summary: The Temple of Lost Coins is a half-ruined former church of Trudd located in the Coins district of Absalom. It is the base of operations of the Forthright, the thieves' guild of the Coins. It is also the residence of the guild master known as the Harlequin.

locations.name: Temple of Sivanah
locations.summary: The Temple of Sivanah of Absalom is located in the Wise Quarter, where knowledge of all sciences and practices is sought. It is a small structure that changes almost imperceptibly each day, and the students of the Arcanamirium who visit it regularly say that its artistic style also changes, although at a less noticeabl...

locations.name: Temple of the Shining Star
locations.summary: Absalom's Temple of the Shining Star, located near the street ringing the pit around the Starstone Cathedral, is the largest temple of Sarenrae north of the capital of Qadira, and the only such church in Absalom.

locations.name: Terrag's Fungi Farm
locations.summary: The Terrag's Fungi Farm has been a business managed and expanded by Ezlip Terrag's family for generations. What began as a cellar has grown into a series of tunnels and caverns where all kinds of subterranean plants are cultivated.

locations.name: Tesyovensku's Warehouse
locations.summary: Tesyovensku's Warehouse is a shop that sells skymetals at very good prices, and many wonder where its mysterious owner, Tesyovensku, gets these materials. The owner has a strange way of moving, sometimes rigid and other times very smooth, and they rarely wants to talk about the reason for this physical affliction.

locations.name: The Clockwork Caravan
locations.summary: The Clockwork Caravan is a series of wagons that roam the Grand Bazaar, driven by the dangerous owner, Sihn Siphandon. The danger doesn't come from him, as he is a kind and polite gentleman, but from the dozens of assassins who are out for his life and who sometimes attack the caravan.

locations.name: The Harrow Barrow
locations.summary: The Harrow Barrow is a traveling shop run by harrow card collector Dieral Myrnese, who roams the streets of Absalom. Following him are several magical wheelbarrows, which move on their own and maintain the extensive card collection he has amassed over years of adventure.

locations.name: The Mask and Moon
locations.summary: The Mask and Moon is a famous restaurant, as is its owner, Leisbarenmia Okavet. It offers diverse cuisine in its establishment, the main part of which is outdoors, and the woodwork features designs reminiscent of those seen on the Mordant Spire.

locations.name: The Menagerie
locations.summary: The Menagerie is a pet shop that caters to the needs of a wide variety of creatures from across the Inner Sea. Darz and Cendra are the lively owners of the shop, which is decorated with various symbols representing natural phenomena. Unfortunately, they face prejudice even in a city as diverse as Absalom.

locations.name: The Resplendent Rose
locations.summary: The Resplendent Rose is a music shop in The Coins that can be found by following the voice of its owner, Ralliadra, whose singing can be heard several shops away.

locations.name: The Rune Room
locations.summary: The Rune Room is a shop that offers a rune-creation service for clothing, which Rakuskuk designs and sells from his stall. The stall resembles a ship's cabin with a large treasure chest where he displays wares and various trinkets from his past as a jink eater in The Shackles; these items hang throughout the stall in s...

locations.name: The Unscathed Blade
locations.summary: The Unscathed Blade is a weapons shop that claims to offer new tools for defeating all kinds of unique enemies. Located in the bustling Grand Bazaar, this shop, which is also the residence of its blacksmith, Abiah, seems quite ordinary at first glance, but the quality of what it sells only becomes apparent when one ste...

locations.name: Third Hand Thrift
locations.summary: Third Hand Thrift is a shop tucked between two buildings, difficult to find in the Grand Bazaar, yet it attracts customers from the Ivy and Petal Districts, despite being a high-end clothing store.

locations.name: Thistleguard Station
locations.summary: The Thistleguard Station is the base from which the Ivy District guard operates. Located north of the Ivy District Park, it has a holding cell for up to 10 criminals to be detained until they are prosecuted.

locations.name: Three Columns Yard
locations.summary: The Three Columns Yard is located in the center of Azlanti Keep, serving as a place to test new weapons and unique fighting styles. Efforts to acquire better techniques for breaking free from grabs or knockdowns are in high demand, following the fierce battles of the Fiendflesh Siege.

locations.name: Thuvian Embassy
locations.summary: The Thuvian Embassy is located in a shady corner of the Petal District in Absalom. The building is ornate, two-story structure with whitewashed walls. As befitting its importance to diplomatic relations, the inside is well decorated with exotic rugs, plush furniture, and works of art.

locations.name: Tiantown
locations.summary: Tiantown is a neighborhood in the Foreign Quarter where most of the Tian Xia immigrants on Absalom reside. Although empires on that continent tend to be long-lasting, their fall results in great trauma for their inhabitants, who then move to Absalom and the most recent wave of migration came with the collapse of Lung W...

The Titan's Fountain is located in the Precipice Quarter of Absalom; it gained its name as at its centre is an enormous, untarnished steel fist that seems as though it is punching its way...

locations.name: To Eat the World
locations.summary: To Eat the World is a famous restaurant in Westgate thanks to its chef, Sammael Rantore, who transforms the process of cooking and serving food into a dramatic spectacle that people even pay to watch.

locations.name: Tomb of the Living
locations.summary: The Tomb of the Living is located in Westgate and is built in the Osirian style. Thanks to the loophole that those who continue to move when entombed can be imprisoned without trial after being buried, the city maintains that this is a tomb, not a prison and its spaciousness allows them to incarcerate enemies of the ci...

locations.name: Tower of Twin Truths
locations.summary: The Tower of Twin Truths is the largest and most important temple of Nethys in Absalom.

locations.name: Tower of the Candelabra
locations.summary: The Tower of the Candelabra is a ruined, flooded structure off the southern coast of the Precipice Quarter in Absalom. The other two towers are the intact Tower of the Broken Shield (colloquially known as Beldrin's Tower) and the fallen Tower of the Horn.

locations.name: Tower of the Horn
locations.summary: This page contains spoilers for the following products: encounter details in Echoes of the Overwatched.You can disable this banner in your personal preferences. The Tower of the Horn is a ruined spire formerly of a magic school located on the Precipice Quarter's cliffside in Absalom.

locations.name: Trawl
locations.summary: The Trawl is an artificial reef in the waters west of the Absalomian town of Diobel. Most of the town's small boats are moored here, and it is home to Mason Karbie, leader of the Barge Gang, along with much of his extended family, and the pleasure barge known as Wisps on the Water.

locations.name: Turning Leaf
locations.summary: The Turning Leaf is a very popular restaurant in Eastgate that focuses on fish and vegetable dishes sourced from the Green Ridge. For two or three days each month, traveling chefs make appearances, preparing specialties from far-flung regions around the world.

locations.name: Tyrant's Grasp
locations.summary: This page contains spoilers for the following products: Midwives to Death.You can disable this banner in your personal preferences. This article is about the location near Absalom. For the Pathfinder Adventure Path, see Tyrant's Grasp (adventure path).

locations.name: Uiry Manor Museum
locations.summary: The Uiry Manor Museum was the residence of this noble family who held considerable influence in the city until 4673 AR. One night, a stranger arrived at the house, invited by the Scion Lord and when the butler went to another manor to get more wine, he returned to find a scene of carnage; everyone was dead, from the no...

locations.name: Ultimate Utensils
locations.summary: Ultimate Utensils is a weapons and armor shop that incorporates kitchen utensils into its designs. The inspiration came from a time when the owner, Uranku, had to defend himself with only a knife and fork, and the dual-purpose nature of the items sold here eliminates the need to carry extra weight from traditional uten...

locations.name: Underdocks
locations.summary: The Underdocks are a network of platforms and passageways beneath Diobel Harbor, used by smugglers. Boats, secret passages, and coral and seaweed that obscure the view make the place quite comfortable for criminals who want to escape the limelight for a while.

locations.name: Union of Carpenters, Stonemasons, and Woodcutters
locations.summary: The Union of Carpenters, Stonemasons, and Woodcutters is located near the center of The Coins district, where the city's finest craftspeople gather and where commissions for projects requiring their talent are received.

locations.name: Unlimited Skewers
locations.summary: Unlimited Skewers is a stall where Shidana uses her skills and dexterity to prepare skewers with flair right in front of her customers, turning the process into a spectacle. Those who visit her in the Grand Bazaar can order custom dishes by providing the ingredients, and she will cook them fabulously to their liking.

locations.name: Urban Garden Jewelers
locations.summary: The Urban Garden Jewelers is a shop concept that only someone from Absalom could have come up with. The idea is to create jewelry using organic plant materials instead of metals, shells, but surprisingly, its quality impresses even the most skeptical socialite.

locations.name: Utterhome
locations.summary: Utterhome is the base of operations for the Sleepless Suns, the guard of Absalom's Foreign Quarter. The structure was a manor in the Osirian style, complete with Jadwiga ice statues, glass panels imported from New Thassilon, Tian Xia-style pools, and Vudrani area gardens, the fortress reflects the district's diversity....

locations.name: Vault of Abadar
locations.summary: For other meanings of "Bank of Abadar", please see Bank of Abadar (disambiguation). The Vault of Abadar, also known as the Bank of Abadar, in Absalom's Ivy District is the most holy site to the faithful of Abadar. While the Vault may appear to be unstable, it is sturdy and solid.

locations.name: Vents
locations.summary: The Vents are the lower reaches of Azlanti Keep in Absalom, where fissues run deep into the earth and vent steam and the small of brimstone. This area consists mostly of abandoned halls and narrow corridors that parallel and bridge the vents, and is connected to the rest of the keep by only four well-guarded rooms.

locations.name: Verdurous Torsion
locations.summary: The Verdurous Torsion is a series of tunnels and caverns beneath the Arboretum Arcanis that after the earthquake that corrupted the magic of the greenhouse, these plants and fungi descended into the earth, spreading their roots and attacking everything in their path.

locations.name: Vert Pippen
locations.summary: The Vert Pippen is a parlor house in the Westgate district of Absalom. The Vert Pippen was one of the bars at which the Pathfinder Society was founded on 23 Desnus, 4307 AR.

locations.name: Vigil's Hope
locations.summary: Vigil's Hope, located in the Precipice Quarter of Absalom, is the headquarters of the Knights of Lastwall and serves as an embassy for the exiled leadership of the destroyed nation of Lastwall.

locations.name: Wachail Estate
locations.summary: The Wachail Estate serves as the residence of the decaying noble family led by Lord Navvem. It was raided in 4720 AR after he refused to free his slaves when the practice was outlawed.

locations.name: Walrus's Way
locations.summary: The Walrus's Way is a series of tunnels beneath the Flying Alderman, named after the nickname of its owner, Drock Ovix whose tusks resemble those of this animal, and those who prove they are members of the Pathfinder Society, usually by showing him their wayfinders, have access to this series of tunnels for whatever th...

locations.name: Wandering Monster
locations.summary: The Wandering Monster is an irregular park maintained by the Ivy District's leshy population. It features an open-air amphitheater that circumvents the rules prohibiting unregistered artists outside the Street Performers and Actors' Guild from performing.

locations.name: Wares... From Beyond!
locations.summary: Wares... From Beyond! is a curiosity shop filled with humanoids with small wings in jars, unnaturally glowing stones, and small tablets with undecipherable inscriptions. The tent is run by the halfling Klart Oswo.

locations.name: Watchtower (Absalom)
locations.summary: The Watchtower is located at the eastern edge of the city, making it the tallest tower on Absalom, surpassing both the Blue Tower and the Pilot Island lighthouse. From this structure, the Cairnlands are monitored, and even the distant Immenwood can be seen.

locations.name: Watercleft
locations.summary: The Watercleft is a cliff on the border between the Petal District and Eastgate, where a spring is moved by aqueducts, creating a beautiful view. There is much social activity in the area as people come to collect water from the spring.

locations.name: Westgate Bathhouse
locations.summary: The Westgate Bathhouse is one of the most popular establishments of its kind in the city, receiving visitors day and night who come to enjoy its spacious pools. The marble structure gives it a cathedral-like feel due to its size, and it offers massage services, a market, and private pools for couples or those plotting...

locations.name: Westgate Heritage Museum
locations.summary: The Westgate Heritage Museum is dedicated to telling the history of the district from its beginnings to the present day, and is criticized by residents of other districts for the clear bias in its tours.

locations.name: White Grotto
locations.summary: White Grotto is the premier bardic college in Absalom where the students learn the art of using magic to enhance all forms of entertainment. The school is located in the upscale Ivy District.

locations.name: Windarium
locations.summary: The Windarium is a clockworks shop in Westgate that is going through difficult times. The shop is located in a shopping district frequented by those looking for parts or repairs. Founded by Symo in 4705 AR, the shop began to gain popularity when he met Mirtion, who had already successfully run several shops.

locations.name: Winking Cyclops Tavern
locations.summary: The Winking Cyclops Tavern is located in the Coins district of Absalom. Its proprietor is Banabus Liventchi.

locations.name: Wisdom's Refuge
locations.summary: Wisdom's Refuge is where the district's Wise Council conducts its administrative activities, focusing on education and the arts. To further their goals, many institutions dedicated to preserving history or knowledge receive reduced taxes, which are then passed on to students at the district's numerous schools and acade...

locations.name: Wisps on the Water
locations.summary: Wisps on the Water is a pleasure barge moored in the Trawl in the Absalomian town of Diobel. It is run by Salodri, and is home to every indulgence of the flesh imaginable and glows with illusory floating lights, which gives the barge its name.

locations.name: Withrun House
locations.summary: The Withrun House is a school founded by Kalistocrats who instill their doctrine in the children of Absalom's wealthiest families, who are unaware of the cult's control. Due to its similarity to the Prophet's Academy, it maintains a rivalry with them. They also have their own team of ruk called the Withrun Wraiths.

locations.name: Wondervale
locations.summary: The Wondervale was created decades after Aroden's death by Absalom's intellectuals, who sought to showcase the city's inventions and demonstrate that it had not declined in relevance after the death of its patron god.

locations.name: Wounded Wisp
locations.summary: This article covers the tavern in Absalom. For the Pathfinder Society Roleplaying Guild scenario, see The Wounded Wisp. The Wounded Wisp is a tavern in the western Foreign Quarter of Absalom. Its proprietor and bartender is Heryn Gale, who inherited the establishment from her father.

locations.name: Wracked Rock
locations.summary: The Wracked Rock is a stony structure in an abandoned block of buildings in the Precipice Quarter, inhabited not out of necessity but because they are drawn by the strange dreams that occur when sleeping near the obelisk.

locations.name: Yargos's Mission
locations.summary: Yargos's Mission is the most reliable charitable organization in The Puddles, where Yargos Gill, the old veteran, puts a portion of his fortune to provide food and medicine to the most unfortunate in the district.

locations.name: Yemhasin
locations.summary: Yemhasin is a neighborhood in Absalom where the Yamasan diaspora goes about their daily lives. Most are farmers, and even if they don't sell their vegetables, they likely have a garden where they grow them for personal use.

locations.name: Zamlin's Drouge Den
locations.summary: Zamlin's Drouge Den is an elegant, jet-black, oceanside two-story inn and gambling house in west-central Diobel run by Talika Zamlin. It specializes in the addictive Vudran game of draj, (locally pronounced "drouge"), and fine spirits.
